name: Stateful Large Language Model Serving with Pensieve
problem: LLM serving systems are stateless across requests, so a growing multi-turn conversation log is re-processed on every turn.
mechanism: Conversation-state caching: keep the already-processed history across requests in a MULTI-TIER cache that uses both GPU and CPU memory, and generalize the PagedAttention kernel to support attention between multiple input tokens against a GPU cache spread over NON-CONTIGUOUS memory (so a cached prefix need not be a single contiguous block). This is a storage/tiling contribution, NOT quantization or sparsity.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): 1.14x-3.0x THE THROUGHPUT OF vLLM AND TensorRT-LLM, and significantly reduced latency, for multi-turn conversation serving. Baseline is explicit and named (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) which makes this one of the better-anchored claims in the serving literature. COMPRESSION RATIO: none - this is reuse, not compression. QUALITY COST: exactly zero, because the cached history is the same computation.
